title: PAIRED RESONANCE
territory: Two substantial filled forms in a conversational relationship, with speech and listening expressed by the open interval between their facing surfaces.
oneSentenceMeaning: One form gives a thought shape; the other makes room to receive it, leaving the original voice present between them.
appIdentity: Mluva makes speaking feel like a natural way to work on Omarchy. A shortcut starts a small, calm recording surface; speech becomes text that can be kept, edited, polished and shaped into useful Markdown. Its delight comes from a responsive rhythm and careful continuity: the original recognition remains available while a working draft develops beside it. The user stays the author. Local and cloud providers are choices within that experience, with speech and rewriting configured independently. Open source gives the product a practical, inspectable character. The identity should feel immediate, capable and quietly personable, comfortable beside a terminal without pretending to be a terminal utility. The promise, Most delightful dictation for Omarchy, is an ambition expressed through daily ease. A little more delight every day gives that ambition a human scale.
markIdentity: Paired Resonance turns the relationship between expression and attention into a compact mark. Two dark, substantial bodies face one another across a continuous open channel. The taller left body carries a generous inward shoulder, suggesting an utterance offered into space. The shorter right body receives that movement with a shallow concavity. Their surfaces acknowledge each other without touching, enclosing a circle or becoming mirror images. This interval is the identity's active part: room for a voice, room for interpretation and room for the user to revise. It also echoes the product's retention of original recognition beside an editable result, without assigning either body to a provider or a processing location. Almost straight outer spines give the mark the composure of a desktop tool. Broad transitions give it warmth. The slight difference in height establishes a conversational rhythm, while the common lower alignment makes the pair feel settled. Its meaning should remain an invitation, rather than a pictogram that must be decoded.
logoDescription:
The final mark consists of exactly two closed, solid shapes, arranged upright in a compact, slightly wide composition. There is no surrounding tile. On a notional 100-unit field, the combined artwork occupies approximately x=6 to 94 and y=10 to 90. The left body reaches the full height. The right begins about twelve units lower, and both finish on the same optical baseline. Each body must read as a broad mass with a substantial interior, never as a bracket, ribbon or thickened stroke. Their widths are close enough to belong together, with the receiving right body gaining a little lower-body fullness to compensate for its shorter height.

The outer sides contain long, almost straight vertical stretches. The upper and lower transitions are rounded with controlled, compact curves. Neither body ends in a point. The left body's facing edge advances into a broad shoulder slightly above the vertical centre, then relaxes inward below it. The right body's facing edge has a shallow receiving hollow at approximately the same height. These are related surfaces, not matching puzzle pieces. The resulting clear channel remains open from top to bottom and shifts gently across the composition around the shoulder. Its narrowest usable width is nine units; the central breathing space expands to roughly fifteen. Avoid a repeated wave, sharp zigzag or closed oval counter.

The most distinctive moment is the shoulder meeting available space. It should suggest the physical generosity of speaking and listening, without drawing a mouth, ear, face, microphone or speech-bubble tail. Preserve a small amount of geometric tension: the outer spines feel composed while the inner edges have one measured exchange. All curve transitions are smooth, but the overall silhouettes retain deliberate structure. Do not turn the forms into liquid droplets, beans or polished stones.

The mark is monochrome, rendered in one fully opaque ink on actual transparent alpha. At 24 pixels, the total drawing should occupy about 22 by 20 pixels and retain an open central passage of roughly two pixels. The unequal heights, substantial bodies and shoulder-to-hollow relationship must survive without surface effects. Large-scale presentation may reveal curve quality, but it must use the same essential geometry. A visual study should compare ink on light and reverse ink on dark while retaining transparency in the exported master. This proposal is study artwork and does not replace the current Mluva identity.
wordmarkDescription:
The wordmark reads exactly Mluva, with an uppercase M and lowercase luva. Start from JetBrains Mono Medium outlines, preserving the family resemblance to Mluva's editable application typography. Then treat the five letters as a short piece of drawn lettering. The result should retain clear construction, an upright stance and the familiar technical calm of the source, while optical spacing removes the mechanical rhythm of equal-width cells. Do not add an icon, descriptor, ligature or ornamental punctuation to the wordmark asset.

Give the M a stable pair of vertical stems and an open internal valley. Lighten the visual accumulation where its diagonals converge without thinning the overall letter. Its width can remain close to the source because it provides the word's opening anchor. Narrow the l substantially, following the established Mluva precedent, while retaining a short, unmistakable foot. The l must remain a lowercase letter rather than becoming an I, numeral one or floating divider. Preserve its clear ascender height and leave enough air after the M for that narrow form to stand independently.

Sculpt the u and v as the wordmark's quiet conversational pair. Give the u a slightly fuller lower bowl and a generous internal opening; soften the v's lowest junction just enough to match the u's optical weight. Keep the v recognisably angular. The relation should be felt in balance, not illustrated by replacing letters with the two logo bodies. Retain a conventional, clearly legible lowercase a from the source construction, opening its small counter and cleaning dense joins where needed. Its terminal should give the word a composed ending rather than a decorative flourish.

Space the five letters by the apparent white intervals between their contours. Begin with tighter Ml and lu than the inherited monospace cells, then inspect uv and va for diagonal gaps that appear larger than measured spacing. The baseline stays level; rounded forms receive only a small optical overshoot. Use solid monochrome filled outlines on actual transparent alpha. At small sizes, Mluva must read immediately and keep its a counter open. The final effect is a familiar tool made more attentive through proportion, with one narrow l and a carefully balanced uv providing its distinguishing character.
selfCritique: The first obvious failure is a pause button. Two upright bodies may be read as a control before they are read as a brand. Unequal heights and a visible shoulder-to-hollow exchange must be present in the silhouette at 24 pixels; if they disappear, the concept has failed rather than merely become more minimal.

Two curved forms can drift toward yin-yang, quotation marks or familiar paired communication logos. A rotational arrangement, equal droplets, circular perimeter or detached dots would make that resemblance worse. The final upright composition needs independent recognition testing; no originality clearance is implied by this written study.

An evocative explanation cannot rescue generic beans. If viewers see two soft objects with no relationship, the inner contours are too vague. The central space needs one legible event, while the outer geometry supplies enough straightness to avoid a liquid or wellness identity.

A perfect convex-concave fit could imply locked processing, automatic completion or a jigsaw product. Mluva preserves a source and permits revision. The shapes therefore need a comfortably open interval and deliberately nonmatching facing surfaces.

The taller left body can dominate, leaving the listener as an accessory. Compensate through right-body fullness and optical area rather than equalising both heights. Confirm balance using a silhouette, not a pleasing colour treatment.

The conversational metaphor may imply a messaging app or an autonomous social assistant. The wordmark and product descriptor will need to establish dictation and rewriting. The symbol should not gain literal bubbles or faces in an attempt to explain the product by itself.

Customising every JetBrains Mono letter would erase continuity and make a five-letter word busy. Restrict the visible character to the narrowed l, lucid M and balanced uv. Small counter corrections and spacing can do more useful work than conspicuous inventions.

The mark cannot honestly promise perfect recognition, wholly local processing or intelligent agreement. Its two bodies communicate attention and retained authorship; any more literal claim would exceed the product contract.
revision: The initial territory risked two mirrored, softly curved comma forms orbiting a narrow S-shaped gap. The revised final abandons that rotational symmetry and makes the pair upright, broad and grounded on one baseline. The left is taller; the shorter right carries more lower-body mass. Long, nearly straight outer spines replace continuous liquid curvature. One broad inward shoulder and one shallow receiving hollow replace repeating waves. The channel is open at both ends, at least nine units wide, and deliberately does not form a closed mouth or interlocking seam. This revision makes the relationship inspectable at small sizes and gives the mark a more credible place in an Omarchy desktop. The wordmark revision also reduces intervention: JetBrains Mono remains recognisable, the l is narrowed, spacing is optical, and the u and v are balanced without becoming miniature logo parts. All descriptions and prompts in this file specify this revised direction.
logoPrompt:
Create one final standalone abstract logo mark for Mluva. LOGO ONLY: absolutely no text, letters, wordmark, caption, numbers, labels, comparison panels, surrounding tile, mockup or scene. Use exactly two substantial CLOSED FILLED bodies in one opaque solid black ink, on actual transparent alpha. Transparency must be real, with no white background and no drawn checkerboard. Flat graphic artwork with precise, smooth vector-like boundaries; no outlines or strokes, gradients, shading, texture, glow, highlights or dimensional effects.

The concept is paired resonance: a voice offered and space made to receive it. Compose two upright, dense forms as a compact pair, slightly wider than tall. In a 100-unit reference field the total mark spans approximately x 6–94 and y 10–90. The left body is taller. The right starts twelve units lower. Both end on one optical baseline. Each is a broad solid mass, never a bracket, ribbon or hollow outline. Give the right a fuller lower body to balance its shorter height. Use long, nearly straight outer spines with controlled rounded ends, no pointed tips. The facing edge of the left form has ONE generous rounded shoulder slightly above the centre. The facing edge of the right has ONE shallow receptive concavity at the same level. Their contours acknowledge one another but do not fit together like a puzzle. Keep an open top-to-bottom channel between them: minimum nine units, opening to about fifteen near the middle, with one gentle lateral shift. No closed counter, S-shaped swirl, repeated waveform or lightning zigzag.

The pair should feel quietly conversational, precise and friendly, built for a modern open-source Omarchy app. Maintain distinctive unequal heights and inner contour structure at a 24-pixel icon scale. Reject anything resembling a pause button, mirrored commas, yin-yang, two water droplets, beans, speech bubbles, parentheses, ears, faces, a microphone or a copied brand. Centre the single mark with generous transparent margins. Render only the revised final geometry, crisp and monochrome.
wordmarkPrompt:
Create one custom wordmark that reads EXACTLY Mluva, uppercase M followed by lowercase luva. WORDMARK ONLY: no logo symbol, icon, descriptor, slogan, label, alphabet specimen, comparison, framing device, application tile, mockup or scene. Use one opaque solid black ink on actual transparent alpha. Transparency must be real, with no painted background and no checkerboard pattern. All letters are filled outline artwork with smooth precise boundaries, not stroked paths. No gradients, shadows, glow, texture, embellishment or dimensional effects.

Begin with JetBrains Mono Medium letter construction and preserve its recognisable upright technical character. Customise the five letters through optical sculpting and spacing rather than using unmodified equal-width text. Keep a stable uppercase M with clear vertical stems and an open central valley; reduce dark congestion at the diagonal joins. Narrow the lowercase l substantially while preserving its ascender and short clear foot. It must look immediately like a lowercase l, never a capital I or numeral one. Make the u's lower bowl slightly fuller and keep its opening generous. Balance the v's weight with the u, gently soften its lowest junction, and retain its angular identity. Keep a conventional, fully legible lowercase a based on the source letter, with an open counter and clean joins. Do not turn the u and v into pictograms or merge any letters.

Use carefully judged proportional optical spacing, particularly a compact but distinct Ml, clear lu, and balanced white intervals around uv and va. Maintain one level baseline with only subtle optical overshoot. Aim for the calm capability of an Omarchy desktop tool and a small amount of warmth through proportion. The exact word must read instantly at small size. Produce one horizontal Mluva wordmark, centred with generous transparent margins, crisp monochrome filled artwork. Do not include the paired-resonance mark.
smallSizeRisks: The open channel can close after downsampling or reverse-colour irradiation. Treat two visible pixels at a 24-pixel canvas as the working minimum, and inspect both ink and reversed output before accepting geometry.
If the shoulder and receiving hollow each become less than about one pixel of visible deviation, the mark becomes two bars. Exaggerate their broad relationship rather than adding detail.
Too much corner rounding makes the smaller right body look like a separate dot or capsule. Keep its height substantial and its lower mass broad.
The shared baseline may seem uneven because one lower curve turns earlier. Judge the pair optically in a monochrome silhouette rather than relying only on coordinate equality.
The narrowed l and the a counter are the wordmark's vulnerable features. Do not reduce the wordmark to the 24-pixel symbol use case; prefer the symbol alone where the full name cannot remain legible.
opticalRules: Exactly two closed filled paths; no detached dots, holes within a body, outlines or background tile.
Nominal combined bounds are 88 units wide by 80 high on a 100-unit construction field, with the right top twelve units lower than the left and both bases optically aligned.
Keep both bodies substantial. Target a perceived left-to-right ink-area balance between 52:48 and 55:45, compensating the shorter body through width and lower fullness.
Keep the central channel continuously open from top to bottom, at least nine units at its narrowest usable point, with a broader central space near fifteen units.
Use one broad shoulder and one shallow receiving hollow. They must not become mirror images, matching puzzle edges, thin brackets or a repeated wave.
Retain long nearly straight outer spines and blunt rounded ends. Avoid a circular overall silhouette, sharp tips, liquid curvature and rotational symmetry.
For 24-pixel review, fit the drawing to approximately 22 by 20 pixels and examine native-size rendering on light and dark grounds without blur or effects.
Build the wordmark from JetBrains Mono Medium outlines, keep exact Mluva casing, narrow the l, preserve ordinary letter recognition and tune spacing by visible gaps.
Use fully opaque single-colour ink. Any inverse version changes only ink colour; exported masters retain actual transparent alpha.
Keep clear space around the mark of at least one quarter of its height. Do not use that clear-space field as a visible rounded square.
motionRelationship: The pair can acknowledge the existing 3.4-second breathing cadence through a restrained opening of the interval, with each body moving outward by no more than one percent of total mark width before settling back. Keep the outer bounds composed, preserve the full minimum gap and avoid scale pumping, liquid deformation, orbiting or an equaliser response. In a brand reveal, the left may become visible a fraction before the right, then both hold together; this is an authored conversational beat, not a claim about recognition latency. The wordmark stays geometrically stable. Reduced motion uses the final static mark immediately. The film's licensed water can remain a separate environmental surface; the mark itself stays flat, solid and visually independent of that footage. This is a study relationship only, with no instruction to replace the current breathing light or app state indicators.
